rounds.fact: Fox News launched its website alongside the cable channel in the mid-90s, and its early design leaned heavily on the bold red-white-and-blue branding that still defines the network today.
Blizzard's late-90s site supported both Diablo and StarCraft, two games that helped define entire genres and whose online play features were unusually ambitious for their time.
Allrecipes built its entire catalog from user-submitted recipes rather than professional chefs, an early example of crowdsourced content outperforming edited, expert-driven sites.
Addicting Games grew rapidly during the mid-2000s Flash gaming boom, hosting thousands of free browser games at a time when installing a game usually still meant buying a physical disc.
Zillow launched in 2006 and was one of the first sites to give the public free access to home value estimates, a feature ('Zestimate') that unsettled a lot of real estate agents at the time.
